standard_prerequisites.name: Extensions of O-modules and their pullback along a map

core_obligations: Build the inverse map: given xi in H^1(C, F), choose an injection F contained in I with I injective in Mod(O) and set Q = I/F; the long exact cohomology sequence then exhibits xi as the image of a global section tilde xi of Q, i.e. of a map O -> Q over the site (proof lines 390-398).

Form the pullback extension: take the pullback of the displayed short exact sequence 0 -> F -> I -> Q -> 0 along tilde xi : O -> Q, which yields the short exact sequence 0 -> F -> E -> O -> 0 together with the map of short exact sequences drawn as a commutative square (proof lines 399-413).

Identify the two constructions: the resulting extension is the candidate inverse of the map 'extension -> image of 1 in H^1(C, F)' described in the statement, the forming of pullbacks being the operation recorded in Homology, Section homology-section-extensions (proof lines 413-414).
proof_roadmap: Construct the inverse: embed F into an injective I, put Q = I/F, and use the long exact cohomology sequence to represent a class xi as a global section of Q (proof lines 390-398).
Pull the extension 0 -> F -> I -> Q -> 0 back along that section, obtaining the extension 0 -> F -> E -> O -> 0 displayed as a commutative square (proof lines 399-413).
Invoke the standard reference for extensions of O-modules to justify that this is the inverse of the map given in the statement (proof lines 413-414).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts a canonical bijection between Ext^1_{Mod(O)}(O, F) and H^1(C, F) which sends an extension 0 -> F -> E -> O -> 0 to the image of 1 in Gamma(C, O) under the connecting map (statement lines 374-386). The proof does not verify the map but constructs its inverse: an injective embedding F contained in I with Q = I/F is chosen, the long exact cohomology sequence identifies the given class with a global section of Q, and that section is used as the map along which the extension 0 -> F -> I -> Q -> 0 is pulled back (proof lines 390-413). What makes this non-formal is that the two directions must be compared through the same connecting map, which is why an injective resolution rather than an arbitrary resolution is used, and the pullback must be organised as a map of short exact sequences to produce the extension. The claim is H2: the construction is short and ends by citing the standard theory of extensions.
